questions.passageText:
**Average Monthly Rainfall (mm) in Three Cities**

| City | Jan | Apr | Jul | Oct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lumen | 82 | 64 | 21 | 70 |
| Corvala | 45 | 51 | 49 | 47 |
| Tessic | 12 | 30 | 96 | 40 |

A geography student claims that one of the three cities receives roughly the same amount of rain in every season.
questions.questionPrompt: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the student's claim?

options.text: Lumen receives 82 mm of rain in January and 21 mm in July.
Corvala's monthly rainfall stays between 45 mm and 51 mm in all four months shown.
Tessic receives more rain in July than either of the other cities.
Each city receives at least 12 mm of rain in every month shown.

questions.explanation: Choice B is correct: Corvala's values (45, 51, 49, 47 mm) vary by only 6 mm, which supports a claim of steady rainfall.

questions.passageText:
![Bar graph of club enrollment, 2020–2023](asset:chart_enrollment)

The graph shows how many students joined a school's robotics club in each year from 2020 to 2023. Enrollment grew every year until 2023, when it fell slightly.
questions.questionPrompt: According to the graph, in which year did enrollment first exceed 40 students?
questions.explanation: The third bar (2022) reaches 50 students, the first value above 40.

options.text: ![Line through the origin rising to the right](asset:graph_choice_a)
![Line through the origin falling to the right](asset:graph_choice_b)

questions.explanation: The line $y = -x$ passes through the origin and falls one unit for every unit it moves right, as in graph B.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.questionPrompt:
![Bar graph of club enrollment, 2020–2023](asset:chart_enrollment)

The graph shows club enrollment of 20, 35, 50 and 42 students for 2020 through 2023. What is the mean enrollment over the four years?

![Bar graph of four values: 45, 30, 20 and 10](data:image/png;base64,)

The bars show 45, 30, 20 and 10 units. The first bar is what percent of the total?
